findings.description: In src/fault_manager.c, fm_submit discards a report when the 36-entry pending queue is full. SWC-SUP-008 requires each detection to be submitted for reporting within 10 ms, but the design does not establish that arrivals and drain time prevent overflow or late submission.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the coincident-report deadline question, then establish an arrival and transmission bound and implement reporting that meets the resulting requirement.

findings.description: SWC-SUP-061 and OP-SWC-011 leave the T_DIAG flow rule unresolved. The design checks at the 5 ms cycle-end phase, although T_DIAG may execute within its 20 ms limit; a timely execution can therefore be reported as a missing checkpoint.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision and align the flow check, timing design and upstream requirements with it.

findings.description: src/time_service.c initializes its accumulated timestamp from timer value zero, but OP-SWU-014 records that the inputs do not establish that the timer runs from reset or that hal_timer_start preserves it. The design does not establish the reset-relative timestamp required by SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003.
findings.requested_change: Establish a supported reset-relative time origin and its preservation by the timer port, or revise the design and its allocation to obtain that time.

findings.description: OP-SWU-011 records that the core clock, CRC throughput and execution times are unavailable. The design therefore cannot substantiate the SWC-SUP-061 execution allocations, the 0.5 ms CRC segment limit or the supervisor processor-time budget.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the clock and execution-time assumptions and provide analysis or measurements establishing the allocated timing and processor budgets.
